rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash, Muhammad ibn Abi Layla, and Abu Bakr in a report from ʿAsim read وجنات in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش ومحمد بن أبي ليلى وأبو بكر في رواية عنه عن عاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a nominative subject with omitted predicate, al-Zamakhshari supplies ثم, while Abu al-Baqa supplies من الكرم, matching ومن النخل.
rows.anchor: أحدها: أنها مرفوعة بالابتداء، والخبر محذوف. واختلفت عبارة المعربين في تقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas estimates ولهم and Ibn ʿAtiyya ولكم; the omitted-predicate construction also parallels وحور عين, whose understood predicate is لهم, and is accepted by Sibawayh, al-Kisaʾi, and al-Farraʾ.
rows.anchor: ونظيره قراءة { وحور عين } [الواقعة: 22]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A delayed omitted predicate can be أخرجناها, inferred from the earlier فأخرجنا; Ibn al-Anbari had already analyzed the phrase this way.
rows.anchor: وقدره متأخرا فقال: أي وجنات من أعناب أخرجناها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq's line raises الخمر although it is the object, understood as والخمر أحلها الطعنة, illustrating delayed coordination with an omitted predicate.
rows.anchor: غداة أحلت لابن أصرم طعنة حصين عبيطات السدائف والخمر

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari also allows coordination on قنوان by proximity: eyes follow brows though they are not plucked, just as grape gardens do not come from palm flowers; the author calls this defense weak and characteristic of adjectival attraction.
rows.anchor: هذا نص مذهب ابن الأنباري أيضا، فتحصل له في الآية مذهبان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Coordination on قنوان is also possible if من النخل does not scope over the gardens: palm clusters and separately produced grape gardens; al-Tabari gives this analysis, Ibn ʿAtiyya weakens it, and Abu al-Baqa objects that grapes do not grow from palms.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر الطبري أيضا هذا الوجه أعني عطفها على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من أعناب is an adjectival phrase modifying جنات; it is nominative with the nominative reading and accusative with the other reading, and depends on an omitted element.
rows.anchor: صفة لجنات فتكون في محل رفع ونصب بحسب القراءتين، وتتعلق بمحذوف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All readers have الزيتون and الرمان in the accusative; they may coordinate with جنات or with نبات, as al-Zamakhshari and Abu al-Baqa explain.
rows.anchor: قوله: { والزيتون والرمان } لم يقرأهما أحد إلا منصوبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya instead coordinates these two nouns with حبا; a later conjunct may attach either to the immediately preceding item or to the first item in the series.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم لك أن في المعطوف الثالث فصاعدا احتمالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: زيتون follows the pattern فيعول, with ت extra and ن original, supported by زتنة for land rich in olives and by the pattern قيصوم; فعلول is absent or rare.
rows.anchor: قالوا: أرض زتنة أي كثيرة الزيتون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: زيت and زيتون are distinct roots despite oil being extracted from olives; زات الطعام means adding oil, زات الرأس means anointing it, and ازدات reflects ت changing to د after ز.
rows.anchor: فإنهما مادتان متغايرتان، وإن كان الزيت معتصرا منه، ويقال: زات طعامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رمان has the pattern فعال with original ن, like عناب and حماض; رمنة describes land rich in pomegranates.
rows.anchor: والرمان وزنه فعال نونه أصلية فهو نظير عناب وحماض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مشتبها is a circumstantial accusative most naturally referring to the nearer الرمان, with an omitted matching state for الزيتون; resemblance concerns color and difference concerns taste.
rows.anchor: قوله: { مشتبها } حال: إما من

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari instead applies both states to both olives and pomegranates, with omitted repeated predicates; he compares the ellipsis with 9:62 and a poetic line.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا نحا الزمخشري فإنه قال:

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The cited poem does not prove omitted predicates: بريئا can predicate of singular, dual, or plural, and can be shared by the pronoun and its conjunct; as two circumstantial states it would need dual agreement.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " فعلى قوله يكون تقدير البيت: كنت منه بريئا

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa says the state applies to the pomegranate and to all the fruits; that is semantically sound if ellipsis is understood, but not as literal syntactic agreement.
rows.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " حال من الرمان ومن الجميع "

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read singular مشتبها; an anomalous reading has متشابها وغير متشابه, with the same sense, since افتعال and تفاعل often share meanings.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على " مشتبها " وقرئ شاذا متشابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إلى ثمره depends on انظروا, which means to look with reflection; إلى is used because this sense includes contemplation.
rows.anchor: وهي بمعنى الرؤية، وإنما تعدت ب إلى لما تتضمنه من التفكر.

rows.speaker: الأخوان، author
rows.claim: The Brothers' double-ḍamma reading ثمر admits four analyses: a singular noun, a plural of plurals, a plural of ثمر, or a plural of ثمرة.
rows.anchor: الباقون: بفتحتين، وقرئ شاذا بضم الأول وسكون الثاني.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis treats ثمر as a singular noun, like طنب or عنق.
rows.anchor: أحدها: أن تكون اسما مفردا كطنب وعنق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis makes ثمر a plural of plurals: ثمر is plural of ثمار, itself plural of ثمرة, comparable to أكم and إكام.
rows.anchor: أنه جمع الجمع فثمر جمع ثمار وثمار جمع ثمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis treats ثمر as a plural of ثمر, by analogy with the two plural forms أسد and أسد.
rows.anchor: والثالث: أنه جمع ثمر كما قالوا: أسد وأسد.

rows.speaker: الفارسي
rows.claim: Al-Farisi prefers reading ثمر as the plural of ثمرة, like خشبة/خشب, أكمة/أكم, and the defective pairs لابة/لوب, ناقة/نوق, ساحة/سوح.
rows.anchor: قال الفارسي: " والأحسن أن يكون جمع ثمرة كخشبة وخشب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority's fatḥ reading الثمر is a collective noun whose singular is ثمرة, like شجر/شجرة, بقر/بقرة, and جزر/جزرة.
rows.anchor: وأما قراءة الجماعة فالثمر اسم جنس مفرده ثمرة كشجر وشجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rare reading with a still second radical either eases the double-ḍamma reading or is a plural of ثمرة; with the latter analysis, ثمر parallels سمر and its broken plural is أثمار.
rows.anchor: وأما قراءة التسكين فهي تخفيف قراءة الأخوين، وقيل: بل هي جمع ثمرة

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr reads the Kahf occurrence with ḍamma and a still م; that is eloquent, though consistency would suggest using it here too, since recitation follows transmission.
rows.anchor: وقد قرأ أبو عمرو الذي في سورة الكهف بالضم وسكون الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Anʿām and Yāsīn, ʿĀsim, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathir, Ibn ʿAmir, and Abu ʿAmr read fatḥ; in al-Kahf, ʿĀsim reads fatḥ, the Brothers and Nāfiʿ/Ibn Kathir/Ibn ʿAmir double ḍamma, and Abu ʿAmr ḍamma with sukūn.
rows.anchor: فعاصم يقرؤه بفتحتين كما يقرؤه في هذه السورة، وفي يس، فاستمر على عمل واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distinction offered for al-Kahf—ḍamma for wealth and fatḥ for edible fruit—cannot explain the readings in al-Anʿām and Yāsīn.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكروا في توجيه الضمتين في الكهف ما لا يمكن أن يأتي في السورتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a parallel reading example, Abu ʿAmr, al-Kisaʾi, and Qunbul read خشب, while the others use ḍamma; the author calls the former reading analogous to the one just discussed.
rows.anchor: والباقون بالضم، فهذه القراءة نظير تيك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذا أثمر is a time adverb for انظروا, either purely temporal or conditional with an omitted or advanced response: when it fruits, look at it.
rows.anchor: وهو يحتمل أن يكون متمحضا للظرف، وأن يكون شرطا، وجوابه محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read ينعه with fatḥa on ي and sukūn on ن; Ibn Muhaysin, also reported from Qatada and al-Dahhak, uses ḍamma, while Ibrahim ibn Abi ʿAbla and al-Yamani read يانعة.
rows.anchor: وهي قراءة قتادة والضحاك. وقرأ إبراهيم بن أبي عبلة واليماني: يانعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الينع with fatḥa or ḍamma is the verbal noun of ripening; fatḥa is Hijazi and ḍamma is used by some Najdis, with variants ينَع and ينوع.
rows.anchor: والينع بالفتح والضم مصدر: ينعت الثمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively الينع is a plural of يانع, like تاجر/تجر and صاحب/صحب; ينعت and أينعت both mean that fruit ripened, in triliteral and quadriliteral forms.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الينع بالفتح جمع يانع كتاجر وتجر وصاحب وصحب

rows.speaker: الحجاج
rows.claim: Al-Hajjaj's phrase رؤوسا قد أينعت وحان قطافها describes heads as ripe and ready to be harvested.
rows.anchor: وقال الحجاج: " أرى رؤوسا قد أينعت وحان قطافها "

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says أينعت means the fruit turned red; the hadith phrase compares a red-born child to الينعة, a red bead said to be carnelian or a kind of it.
rows.anchor: قاله الفراء، ومنه الحديث في الملاعنة: " إن ولدته أحمر مثل الينعة "

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayd says ينعت تينع has fatḥa in the past and kasra in the present, citing a line about olives ripening; al-Layth reverses the vowels.
rows.anchor: وقال الليث بعكس هذا: أي بكسرها في الماضي وبفتحها في المستقبل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The close addresses believers because the signs show one God's power to create varied products from one soil and water; only reflective believers benefit from them.
rows.anchor: كون ما تقدم دالا على وحدانيته وإيجاده المصنوعات المختلفة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The hamza in أو من كان may be advanced before the conjunction, the majority analysis, or remain in place with an omitted verb between it and الواو.
rows.anchor: قد تقدم أن هذه الهمزة يجوز أن تكون مقدمة على حرف العطف وهو رأي الجمهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من is the initial subject and كمن its predicate; يمشي is an adjective of نورا, while مثله is the subject and في الظلمات its predicate within من's relative clause.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { أو من كان }: " أو من كان " قد تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The كاف phrase is the predicate of the first من; ليس بخارج is a circumstantial clause describing the relative person as still settled in darkness.
rows.anchor: في محل نصب على الحال من الموصول أي: مثل الذي استقر في الظلمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa attaches the circumstantial clause to the pronoun in منها, barring attachment to the ه in مثله because the predicate intervenes; Makkī attaches it to the implicit pronoun in الظلمات.
rows.anchor: ليس بخارج في موضع الحال من الضمير في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talha ibn Musarrif reads أفمن with فاء instead of واو.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف " أفمن كان " بالفاء بدل الواو.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كذلك زين is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun; estimates compare the unbelievers' beautification either with bringing believers to life or with their remaining in darkness.
rows.anchor: نعت لمصدر فقدره بعضهم: زين للكافرين تزيينا كما أحيينا المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted agent of زين may be God or Satan; both are explicitly named as beautifiers elsewhere in the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: والفاعل المحذوف من " زين " المنوب عنه هو الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما كانوا يعملون occupies the نائب الفاعل position; ما may be a relative pronoun, a verbal noun particle, or an indefinite noun described by a clause, with ellipsis of the relative in the first and third analyses.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون موصولة اسمية أو حرفية أو نكرة موصوفة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses the كاف in the nominative and paraphrases: just as what was related to you, the unbelievers' deeds were beautified.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: " موضع الكاف رفع، و المعنى: مثل ذلك الذي قصصنا عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يوم may depend on an omitted اذكر or on the omitted speech governing the vocative; al-Zamakhshari instead estimates an omitted event: on that day occurred what defies description.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن ينتصب بفعل مقدر فقدره أبو البقاء تارة

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh prefers the proposed parsing over al-Zamakhshari's because his requires deletion of two clauses, including the verb governing the time phrase.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وما قلناه أولى " يعني من كونه منصوبا ب

rows.speaker: الزجاج، الشيخ
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj makes the phrase passive, يقال لهم يا معشر; the Shaykh finds this apt, in keeping with the Qur'anic description that God does not speak to them or purify them.
rows.anchor: وقدره الزجاج بفعل قول مبني للمفعول: يقال لهم يا معشر يوم نحشرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يوم may also depend on وليهم, understood as: He takes charge of them for what they did and takes charge of them on the day they are gathered.
rows.anchor: لما فيه من معنى الفعل أي: وهو يتولاهم بما كانوا يعملون

rows.speaker: بعض النحويين
rows.claim: جميعا is either a circumstantial accusative or, according to some grammarians, an emphatic expression.
rows.anchor: حال أو توكيد على قول بعض النحويين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hafs reads يحشرهم with third-person ياء, referring back to ربهم.
rows.anchor: بياء الغيبة ردا على قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يا معشر is accusative under the omitted يقول or قلنا; with al-Zajjaj's passive صيغة, it is nominative as نائب الفاعل.
rows.anchor: في محل نصب بذلك القول المضمر أي: يقول أو قلنا، وعلى تقدير الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: معشر means a group; an Arabic line uses it for the people from whom the speaker defends others.
rows.anchor: والمعشر: الجماعة قال: 2056 وأبغض من وضعت إلي فيه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet's saying نحن معاشر الأنبياء uses معاشر for a class or group, and states that prophets do not leave inheritance.
rows.anchor: كقوله عليه السلام: " نحن معاشر الأنبياء لا نورث "

rows.speaker: الأودي
rows.claim: Al-Awdi's verse uses معاشر as the plural of معشر, for a group who restore what their people have spoiled.
rows.anchor: وقال الأودي: 2057 فينا معاشر لن يبنوا لقومهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من الإنس may be a circumstantial phrase: their allies were human.
rows.anchor: في محل نصب على الحال أي: أولياءهم حال كونهم من الإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively من identifies the kind, since their allies included humans and jinn, with the phrase specifying the human allies.
rows.anchor: لبيان الجنس؛ لأن أولياءهم كانوا إنسا وجنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ربنا has an omitted vocative particle.
rows.anchor: وربنا حذف منه حرف النداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read أجلنا in the singular, matching الذي; an alternative has آجالنا plural while الذي remains singular and masculine.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على " أجلنا " بالإفراد لقوله

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli treats الذي as generic, with the masculine singular standing for a feminine relative form.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو علي: " هو جنس أوقع الذي موقع التي "

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh instead parses الذي as an appositive, implicitly الوقت الذي; this makes it generic without a mismatch that would prevent an adjectival analysis.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وإعرابه عندي بدل كأنه قيل: الوقت الذي

rows.speaker: الفارسي
rows.claim: Al-Farisi makes خالدين a circumstantial accusative governed by مثواكم, which here is a verbal noun meaning your remaining, not a place noun; he rejects al-Zajjaj's locative gloss.
rows.anchor: قال الفارسي: " المثوى عندي في الآية اسم المصدر دون المكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Farisi's poetic evidence uses مغار ابن همام as a verbal event; its على complement fits an action rather than a place, supporting his verbal-noun reading of مثوى.
rows.anchor:
ومثل هذا قول الشاعر:
2058 وما هي إلا في إزار وعلقة
مغار ابن همام على حي خثعما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second possible governor is an omitted verb, يثوون فيها خالدين, with مثواكم understood as the place of remaining.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أن العامل فيها فعل محذوف، أي: يثوون فيها خالدين

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa proposes the meaning of the possessive construction as the governor; the author rejects this because the meaning of an iḍāfa cannot govern.
rows.anchor: قاله أبو البقاء أن العامل معنى الإضافة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority take the exception from the immediately preceding clause, النار مثواكم خالدين فيها.
rows.anchor: فقال الجمهور: هو الجملة التي تليها وهي قوله { النار مثواكم خالدين فيها }

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim instead makes the exception from their statement that they reached the appointed term: it excludes those whom God seized before that term for disbelief and error.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم: " هو مستثنى من قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects Abu Muslim's antecedent: the wording should then be شئت to match أجلت, and the intervening judgment about the fire improperly separates exception from its antecedent.
rows.anchor: أما الصناعة فمن وجهين أحدهما: أنه لو كان الأمر كذلك لكان التركيب إلا ما شئت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also rejects Abu Muslim's interpretation because it assumes two terms, an early term of seizure and a separately appointed term, which he says is disproved elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وأما المعنى فلأن القول بالأجلين: أجل الاخترام والأجل المسمى باطل لدلائل مقررة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makkī and Abu al-Baqa in one view call this a disconnected exception: the fire is their abode, except those who believed in worldly life, by analogy with 44:56; the author finds this remote.
rows.anchor: فذهب مكي بن أبي طالب وأبو البقاء في أحد قوليهما إلى أنه منقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others regard the exception as connected to the addressed pronoun in مثواكم: those among the group who believed in worldly life are excluded; ما can refer to a rational kind or class.
rows.anchor: وذهب آخرون إلى أنه متصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For this connected reading, ما can apply to a rational class, as in the Qur'anic phrase فانكحوا ما طاب لكم من النساء.
rows.anchor: فانكحوا ما طاب لكم من النسآء [النساء: 3]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The connected exception is questioned because the unbelievers' future punishment and believers' past worldly faith do not share the same time of judgment, as ordinary exceptions require.
rows.anchor: ولكن قد استبعد هذا من حيث إن المستثنى مخالف للمستثنى منه في زمان الحكم عليهما

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Some take the excepted interval as time in the graves; al-Tabari instead makes it the period from resurrection until entry into Hell, since مثواكم need not refer only to the future.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو المدة التي بين حشرهم إلى دخولهم النار، وهذا قول الطبري

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes the exception as the combined duration in the graves and the period after resurrection before entering Hell.
rows.anchor: هو مجموع الزمانين أي: مدة إقامتهم في القبور

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the exception marks intervals when the damned are moved from Hell to a valley of extreme cold that tears their limbs; they howl and ask to return.
rows.anchor: يخلدون في عذاب النار الأبد كله إلا ما شاء الله إلا الأوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify the exception as monotheist sinners who enter Hell but do not remain there forever; ما applies to a category of rational people, and the author says the exception is real and apparent.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: " إلا ما شاء الله هم العصاة الذين يدخلون النار من أهل التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says this is a genuine exception: the apparent meaning is clear and should not be replaced with a figurative threat that presents an unreal event as real.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا استثناء حقيقة، بل يجب أن يكون كذلك.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats the exception as an ironic intensified threat, like a victimized avenger claiming he will relent only if his enemy wishes it.
rows.anchor: وزعم الزمخشري أنه يكون من باب قول الموتور الذي ظفر بواتره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects al-Zamakhshari's metaphorical account as unnecessary, since the exception has an apparent literal sense.
rows.anchor: قلت: ولا حاجة إلى ادعاء ذلك مع ظهور معنى الاستثناء فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri says the exception is the time they spent in the world before punishment; the author considers this even farther from the preceding readings.
rows.anchor: فجعل المستثنى زمن حياتهم وهو أبعد مما تقدم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ, followed by al-Zajjaj, interprets the exception as an increase in punishment; another view says an added form of chastisement, readings that work only as disconnected exceptions.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: وإليه نحا الزجاج

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh parses these as a disconnected exception from the implicit verbal noun: they remain in Hell's punishment except for extra torment beyond the torment denoted by fire.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وهذا راجع إلى الاستثناء من المصدر الذي يدل عليه معنى الكلام

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says this addresses the Prophet and community, not the Judgment scene: it excludes present unbelievers who God knows will later believe, as indicated by حكيم عليم.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " ويتجه عندي في هذا الاستثناء أن يكون مخاطبة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh calls Ibn ʿAtiyya's reading good, but notes he had earlier called the direct divine address the apparent reading; no strong clue justifies departing from it.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وهو تأويل حسن وكان قد قال قبل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting على الذين هادوا before حرمنا marks restriction for some grammarians, including al-Zamakhshari and al-Razi; al-Razi explicitly notes the governed phrase precedes its verb.
rows.anchor: متعلق بحرمنا، وهو يفيد الاختصاص عند بعضهم كالزمخشري والرازي

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The common recitation uses ظفر, which the author calls the highest of five Arabic forms for the word.
rows.anchor: وفي " الظفر " لغات خمس، أعلاها: ظفر وهي قراءة العامة

rows.speaker: الحسن، أُبَيّ بن كعب، الأعرج
rows.claim: A form with sukūn on the middle radical, easing the form with ḍamma, is read by al-Hasan in one report, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, and al-Aʿraj.
rows.anchor: وظفر بسكون العين وهي تخفيف المضمومها، وبها قرأ الحسن في رواية وأبي بن كعب والأعرج

rows.speaker: أبو السمال
rows.claim: A form with kasra on both ظاء and فاء is attributed by al-Wahidi to Abu al-Sammal.
rows.anchor: وظفر بكسر الظاء والفاء، ونسبها الواحدي لأبي السمال قراءة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Another form has kasra on ظاء and sukūn on فاء, easing the kasra; readers also attribute this recitation to al-Hasan.
rows.anchor: وظفر بكسر الظاء وسكون الفاء وهي تخفيف المكسورها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أظفور is a fifth lexical form, though the author knows of no recitation using it; a poetic line attests the word.
rows.anchor: واللغة الخامسة أظفور ولم يقرأ بها فيما علمت، وأنشدوا على ذلك قول الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The triliteral plural is أظفار; أظافير is the regular plural of أظفور, while أظافر without long ا is irregular.
rows.anchor: وجمع الثلاثي أظفار، وجمع أظفور أظافير وهو القياس، وأظافر من غير مد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic fragment, العينين والعواور, is cited as a parallel for the non-analogical plural pattern.
rows.anchor: وأظافر من غير مد وليس بقياس، وهذا كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من البقر may coordinate with كل ذي and attach to the first حرمنا, with the second clause explaining the partitive phrase; or it may attach to the later حرمنا.
rows.anchor: فيه وجهان أحدهما: أنه معطوف على

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa forbids attaching من البقر to the second verb; the Shaykh rejects that restriction, distinguishing its position after the verb from an alleged required position after the object and allowing either order.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وكأنه توهم أن عود الضمير

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh supports the order with examples ضرب غلام المرأة أبوها and غلام المرأة ضرب أبوها: a prepositional phrase and object can exchange order without violating grammatical rank.
rows.anchor: فليس بممنوع بل يجوز ذلك كما جاز: " ضرب غلام المرأة أبوها "
